stories.title: TrackerClient Protocol + get_tracker_client() factory
stories.user_story: As a symphony-workflow maintainer, I want a TrackerClient Protocol and a get_tracker_client() factory, so that orchestrator.py and poller.py can depend on a tracker-agnostic interface instead of being hardcoded to JiraClient.
acceptance_criteria: tracker.py defines TrackerError (a common base exception), ConfigError, and a @runtime_checkable TrackerClient Protocol covering exactly the run-loop's real surface: get_myself, get_issue, add_comment, transition_issue, search_ready_tickets, issue_url, plus close()/context-manager support -- no more, no less.

get_tracker_client() reads SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER (jira|linear, default jira so existing deployments are unaffected) and lazily imports only the selected backend's module, so importing tracker.py never requires both backends' dependencies to be installed.
client.py's JiraError now subclasses tracker.TrackerError, and JiraClient satisfies TrackerClient structurally with zero changes to its class hierarchy (per spec.md: 'a Protocol, not a base class').
client.py gains issue_url() and search_ready_tickets(max_results) methods; the JQL READY_JQL/JIRA_PROJECT construction that previously lived in poller.py moves here.
test_tracker.py covers the factory's env-var switch (jira vs linear vs unset/default) and its lazy-import behavior; existing test_client.py tests still pass unmodified in spirit.

tasks.description: Mocked/parametrized coverage of get_tracker_client()'s env-var branching and lazy-import behavior, plus a Protocol-conformance check that JiraClient satisfies TrackerClient.

stories.title: LinearClient implementation (Linear GraphQL backend)
stories.user_story: As a symphony-workflow operator whose issues live in Linear, I want a LinearClient that implements the TrackerClient surface, so that the Plan/Implement run-loop can drive a Linear team's issues the same way it already drives Jira issues.
acceptance_criteria: linear_client.py implements get_myself, get_issue, add_comment, transition_issue, search_ready_tickets, issue_url, and close()/context-manager against Linear's GraphQL API -- explicitly no create_issue and no arbitrary search (out of scope per intent.md's non-goals).

config.py gains LinearConfig, reading LINEAR_API_KEY (deliberately reusing the same env var name another internal tool's Linear tooling already uses -- one Linear key per machine) and SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_LINEAR_TEAM (team key upper-cased on load).
models.py gains Issue.from_linear and CurrentUser.from_linear classmethods parsing Linear's GraphQL response shapes, added alongside (not replacing) the existing Jira from_api classmethods.

get_issue/add_comment/transition_issue each resolve the human-readable key to Linear's internal UUID via one extra GraphQL round-trip per call (LinearClient._resolve_issue_ids()), deliberately uncached given a Run's low call volume.
transition_issue additionally resolves the issue's team id to look up that team's workflow states, since Linear states are scoped per-team rather than effectively-global the way Jira's are.

search_ready_tickets expresses 'ready to work' as a state-category filter (state: {type: {eq: "unstarted"}}) plus parent: {null: true} to exclude sub-issues -- the structural analog of Jira's issuetype-exclusion JQL, per spec.md's comparison table, not a literal status-name match.
test_linear_client.py mocks every GraphQL call via respx and covers all six TrackerClient methods plus the UUID/team-id resolution round-trips; test_config.py gains LinearConfig test cases.

tasks.description: respx-mocked tests for all six TrackerClient methods, the UUID resolution round-trip, and the team/workflow-state lookup used by transition_issue; add corresponding LinearConfig cases to test_config.py.

stories.title: Migrate orchestrator.py and poller.py to TrackerClient
stories.user_story: As a symphony-workflow maintainer, I want the shared Plan/Implement run-loop logic in orchestrator.py and poller.py to be typed against TrackerClient/TrackerError instead of JiraClient/JiraError, so that api.py and poller.py can drive either backend through the exact same run-loop code without drifting.
acceptance_criteria: orchestrator.py's execute_plan/execute_implement (and any other client-typed signatures) are typed against TrackerClient and catch TrackerError, not JiraError specifically.

render_run_doc's client.base_url + hand-built /browse/{key} construction is replaced with client.issue_url(key); newly-written docs/runs/<key>/plan.md frontmatter renames its jira_url: key to tracker_url: (a deliberate breaking change to the local schema, per spec.md -- historical run docs keep their original jira_url: key unchanged).

poller.py is typed against TrackerClient/TrackerError; its module-level READY_JQL/JIRA_PROJECT constants are removed, and tick() calls self._client.search_ready_tickets(max_results=...) instead of assembling JQL itself.

Existing tests are updated in place, not skipped -- e.g. test_render_run_doc_prepends_jira_url_frontmatter becomes ..._tracker_url_frontmatter -- and continue to pass with JiraClient as the concrete implementation under test.

stories.title: cli.py tracker-agnostic / Jira-only command split
stories.user_story: As a symphony-workflow CLI user, I want get/comment/transition/plan/implement to work against whichever backend SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER selects, while search/call/list-tools/decompose/sync-decomposition stay explicitly Jira-only, so that I get a correct, tracker-agnostic CLI without silently pointing a Jira-only command at a Linear deployment.
acceptance_criteria: cli.py splits its client-construction helper into a tracker-agnostic _client() (backed by get_tracker_client()) and a new _jira_client() (unconditionally JiraClient).
get, comment, transition, plan, and implement subcommands use _client() and behave identically regardless of SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER's value.
search, call, list-tools, decompose, and sync-decomposition subcommands use _jira_client() and remain explicitly Jira-typed, unaffected by SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER.
test_cli.py covers both helpers, including a SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER=linear scenario proving the tracker-agnostic commands don't require Jira-specific env vars to run.

tasks.description: Add/adjust tests covering both helpers, including exercising a tracker-agnostic command under SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER=linear and confirming the Jira-only commands are unaffected by the env var.

stories.title: api.py tracker-agnostic / Jira-only endpoint split + health rename
stories.user_story: As an operator of the FastAPI server, I want tracker-agnostic endpoints to work against either backend and the Jira-only endpoints to fail loudly with a 501 when the deployment isn't Jira, so that a Linear deployment can't be silently routed into tools.py's Jira-shaped handlers.
acceptance_criteria: app.state.jira_client is renamed to app.state.tracker_client; a new get_tracker() dependency backs the tracker-agnostic endpoints (/health, /issues/{key}, /runs/{id}/plan, /runs/{id}/implement).

get_jira_client() performs an isinstance check and raises HTTP 501 for /tools and /tools/{name}/call when the configured backend isn't Jira, instead of passing the wrong client type into tools.py's handlers and failing confusingly deep inside a GraphQL client with no create_issue method.

HealthResponse.jira_reachable is renamed to tracker_reachable, and /health reports it based on whichever backend is actually configured (a deliberate breaking change to the response shape, not additive, per spec.md).

test_api.py covers tracker-agnostic endpoints under both jira and linear configuration, and asserts a 501 (not a 200 or an unhandled exception) from /tools and /tools/{name}/call when SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER=linear.

stories.title: Docs: describe the backend switch honestly
stories.user_story: As a new deployer of symphony-workflow, I want README.md, CLAUDE.md, and docs/PORTABILITY.md to accurately describe SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER and what does and doesn't work on each backend, so that I don't assume Linear feature parity (decompose, sync-decomposition, raw search) that this Epic explicitly didn't build.
acceptance_criteria: README.md documents SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_TRACKER=jira|linear and the Linear-specific env vars (LINEAR_API_KEY, SYMPHONY_WORKFLOW_LINEAR_TEAM) alongside the existing Jira env var table.

docs/PORTABILITY.md gains a Linear-specific walkthrough (pointing a deployment at a real Linear team) and explicitly restates intent.md's non-goals -- no decompose, no sync-decomposition, no raw search, no Epic/parent/sprint/story-points fields -- so operators don't assume feature parity with the Jira path.

CLAUDE.md's description of the tracker split (TrackerClient Protocol, tracker.py, the jira|linear switch) is checked against the actually-shipped code for accuracy, not left as an aspirational description written before implementation.

No doc references the old jira_reachable /health field name or the old jira_url: plan.md frontmatter key as if they were still current -- both are described using their renamed tracker_reachable / tracker_url: forms.

definition_of_done: Unit tests added for all new/changed code; HTTP calls mocked with respx — no live Jira access in tests (CLAUDE.md “the three non-negotiables” #3).

If a Jira operation was added or changed: a typed client.py method AND a matching tools.py Tool entry (pydantic args model), both reachable via `symphony-workflow list-tools`/`call` (CLAUDE.md “the three non-negotiables” #2).
A Typer CLI subcommand added only if a human needs a friendly entry point for it — not every tool needs one (CLAUDE.md “Adding a new tool”, step 4).
`uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` both pass clean (CLAUDE.md “Code style”).
`uv run pytest` passes in full (CLAUDE.md “the three non-negotiables” #3).
Type hints on all new code; pydantic models for anything crossing a boundary such as an HTTP response or tool input (CLAUDE.md “Code style”).
No bare `except Exception: pass`; typed exceptions (e.g. JiraError) caught specifically (CLAUDE.md “Code style”).

No org-specific values (cloud-f1.atlassian.net, CF1 field IDs, ADLC, a hardcoded target-repo path) baked into client.py/orchestrator.py/poller.py — configuration goes through env vars (CLAUDE.md “What NOT to do here”).
